headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: dexter’s broad network/API access can expose sensitive financial context while the prompt-engineering repo offers no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runnable surface or I/O, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. Profile B has autonomous execution and file/API surfaces, but there is no documented shared channel between them. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so the pathway exists but is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B’s output into A-derived prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF both are connected through a shared clipboard, queue, or filesystem, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into prompt templates.
Add a provenance label to any text moved from B to A.
Review any shared clipboard or message queue configuration.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile B explicitly touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, so sensitive context can leave the local environment. Profile A is a non-runnable prompt-engineering repository with no data-handling controls, so pairing it with B does not add protection. The interaction is indirect, but the documented egress makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF B processes financial or market data while network egress remains enabled, data can leave the environment.
IF A is used to author prompts that include B’s sensitive outputs, those outputs may be copied into external services.
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive datasets.
Disable or proxy outbound API calls for B.
Redact financial identifiers before any prompt-writing workflow.
Store B outputs in a separate restricted workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile B supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while A is a repository artifact with no write controls. There is no evidence of locking or coordination, so if both are pointed at the same workspace or scratchpad, write conflicts are plausible. Uncertainty about A’s operational surface does not reduce the risk because the shared-write pathway is not blocked.
conditions: IF multiple B instances share the same .dexter/scratchpad/ directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF A is placed in the same mutable workspace as B, file overwrites or confusion can occur.
mitigations: Assign each instance a unique scratchpad path.
Run only one writer per workspace.
Make the A repo read-only during B runs.
Check for stale lockfiles before execution.
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile B runs autonomously and can act on outputs from upstream steps, while A is a prompt-engineering content source that may be treated as authoritative guidance. There is no documented verification layer between them, so if A-derived instructions or examples feed B, errors can propagate into B’s actions. The lack of direct evidence pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF B consumes A-authored prompts or examples without review, incorrect guidance can propagate.
IF B is configured to execute autonomous workflows from those inputs, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require human review of A-derived prompts before B uses them.
Add a verification step between A output and B execution.
Limit B to read-only analysis mode for trial runs.
Log prompt provenance for every B action.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Profile B explicitly handles financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, which creates compliance exposure around retention, residency, and vendor sharing. Profile A is a public open-source repository with no data-class handling, so it is not the compliance driver here. Because only B is relevant, A is not cited for the substantive compliance risk beyond being non-constraining.
conditions: IF B processes regulated financial data through third-party APIs, retention and sharing obligations apply.
IF any EU or customer-restricted data is routed through B’s external services without a DPA, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm vendor DPAs for each API.
Avoid sending regulated records to external APIs.
Set short retention on logs and scratchpad files.
Document data residency for each service.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
